sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
On Door is a growing regional grocery retailer, not a demonstrated capital-light compounding platform. FY2026 sales reached ₹320.46 crore, but the most important question is whether reported inventory, receivables and earnings support reliable cash economics. The clean main audit and IFC opinion coexist with explicit CARO verification limitations and an intangible accounting policy that is inconsistent with the stated AS26 basis. This is sufficient for a financial-reliability Hold, not an allegation of fraud.

No ordinary expected return, entry price or investment ranking is assigned. BQS, Growth Quality Score and Investment Attractiveness Score are NS because critical factors remain unscored. CASH is 1 and a persistent weak-cash ceiling of 5 applies to the GQS diagnostic bound. The ₹251 official close is dated 15 October 2026, not an authenticated 20 October executable price.

Known funding is real: ₹21.08964 crore equity and ₹7.8 crore warrant upfront receipts in June/July 2026. That supports a cautious plan, but not an assumption that the entire ₹60.4 crore proposed program or optional ₹23.4 crore warrant balance is already financed. The conditional base model ends at ₹387.06 per share, with return 9.05% only if all financial-reliability premises resolve and every required interval funds. This is not a buy recommendation.

sections.text:
Company: On Door Concepts Limited. CIN L52100MP2014PLC033570; NSE SME symbol ONDOOR; ISIN INE00ER01015. Research cutoff 20 October 2026. Financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not IndAS. Latest full audited year ends 31 March 2026. The March 2026 investor presentation supplies rounded H1FY2026 comparatives; no September 2026 results or invented TTM have been used. No subsidiaries, JV or associate are disclosed.

G1 integrity/minority protection: Conditional. G2 financial reliability: Hold. G3 funding/survival: Conditional. G4 tradability: Conditional. Each gate has a specific clearance test in the embedded register. Main opinion, CARO, IFC, Rule 11, notes and subsequent-event evidence were considered separately. Company statements that stock and debtors are good are counterevidence, not independent verification.

Primary documentary confidence is high for dated allotments and the observed exchange rows. Reliability of the economic capital base is low to medium. The base model is an analyst scenario, not company guidance. Model horizon is 20 October 2026–20 October 2031,1826 days divided by 365.25. sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
All 13 factors are audited with evidence, counterevidence, confidence, anchor and upgrade/downgrade conditions. GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH1, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. Unknown is never imputed as 5 or zero. A high score is not awarded for a good story, prospective TAM or a cheap headline multiple.

BQS weights: GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH1 0%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. GQS weights: REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH1 0%. IAS weights: unrounded final BQS 25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10%. Exact Decimal contributions, coverage, raw bounds and capped final bounds appear below and in canonical data. GQS means Growth Quality, not governance; P means price-implied expectations.

No composite is rankable. The CASH1 ceiling of 5 is applied to the GQS diagnostic upper bound even though its point remainsNS. A material G2 Hold excludes ordinary rankings regardless of whether an optimistic missing-factor bound might cross a classification threshold. These bounds are uncertainty ranges, not alternative scores or recommendations.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
On Door sells groceries, FMCG, fresh products and household items through a regional store/franchise, online and B 2 B network. Food demand is frequent and non-discretionary, but margins are thin and working capital sits substantially with the issuer. Under its stated principal assessment, inventory risk and pricing discretion support gross sales recognition. Franchise commission is a cost; this is not merely a royalty stream with franchisee-funded inventory.

The footprint progressed from 55 stores inMarch 2023, including 17 company-owned and 38 franchised, to 63 inMarch 2024 and 65 inSeptember 2025. The store formats are generally small neighborhood outlets, alongside warehouse and technology support. Cluster expansion in Madhya Pradesh can lower replenishment distance and improve brand familiarity, but public disclosure does not give mature/new store cohorts, closures, shrinkage, sales per square foot, online fulfillment contribution or cash payback.

All-in store economics must include rent, staff or franchise commissions, marketing, wastage, maintenance, inventory, supplier advances and distribution infrastructure. Dividing company revenue by ending store count would conflate online/B 2 B and partial-year openings; the report does not call that figure same-store sales. The forecast uses clearly labelled store-equivalent units as a scale device, not asserted actual unit economics.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Convenience, regional density and supplier relationships are useful but contestable advantages. Customers can compare commodity staples and switch easily. Larger chains have procurement scale, while quick-commerce competitors contest delivery frequency and convenience. No independently evidenced switching cost, network lock-in or sustained excess return supports a high moat score.

Avenue Supermarts reported 500 stores atMarch 2026 and Q4 standalone revenue ₹17,204.50 crore, orders of magnitude beyond this issuer. Reliance reported ₹328,202 crore retail revenue from operations and 20,160 stores across formats. These are competitive scale references, not direct valuation comparables. Their owned/leased property mix, formats and IndAS lease accounting differ from On Door’s postrent AS19 presentation.

Spencer’s is a useful adverse reference: FY26 consolidated sales fell 9.8% to ₹1,800 crore and PBT was a ₹250 crore loss despite better gross margin and lower operating costs. Grocery demand alone does not protect shareholder returns. No peer multiple is copied into the model; the 7/10/12× postrent EBITDA scenario multiples are transparent analyst assumptions tested further at 7/10/13×.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue rose from ₹182.6518 crore inFY2021 to ₹320.4628 crore inFY2026, a preferred five-year CAGR 11.9002%. FY2022 was lower at ₹173.1409 crore. FY2023–26 CAGR 21.1672% and FY2024–26 CAGR 17.1470% show recovery, but selecting the best recent window would overstate demonstrated persistence. REV starts at 6 in the 10–15% band and receives no trajectory adjustment.

Recent annual growth is meaningful, yet its decomposition into price, same-store volume, new outlets, online/B 2 B and franchise conversion is not disclosed. No acquisition is identified in the reviewed capital/business record. Gross principal treatment is consistent with the issuer’s stated inventory risk, but it does not prove a comparable same-store volume series. The March 2026 presentation’s H1FY26 sales ₹136 crore versus ₹121 crore are rounded figures, not a precise 13-digit growth input.

The complete six-year historical table, cashflow adjustments and source reconciliation are embedded. FY23 annual versus prospectus differences remain visible. FY25 annual revenue ₹273.0107 crore controls over an inconsistent initial-results comparator. A small starting footprint is not separately penalized after measuring the full five-year period; the limitation is visibility into underlying productivity and cash conversion.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
There is room to add neighborhood clusters, but opportunity must be funded at attractive incremental returns. The report constructs operating invested capital both from assets and from equity/debt less non-operating assets. PPE, intangible assets, deposits and operating working capital are reconciled; residuals are only rounding atFY25–26. Multi-year incremental NOPAT/IC bridges are shown, using 25% normalized cash tax and a 10-year illustrative intangible charge.

CAP remainsNS for a substantive reason: the auditor cannot independently establish inventory, debtor/payable ageing is absent and ₹25.5286 crore of unamortised intangible assets rests on an unsupported indefinite-life policy. Those items materially affect both the capital denominator and recurring earnings. Lack of private store cohorts alone would not forceNS if a reliable stable-organic aggregate bridge existed. Compare any later corrected incremental return with a reasoned 12–15% nominal capital-cost range, not with current headlineROCE.

FY24–26 postinterest financing-neutral CFO totals-₹25.4637 crore and cash capex ₹12.6602 crore. Supplier advances and inventory consume funds even under a franchise format. The new model links store-equivalent openings, first-year sales drag, mature-unit growth, rent escalation, tax, maintenance capex, opening capex and incremental working capital. Base terminal revenue is ₹553.87 crore, which is an assumption-dependent path, not a target. Faster rollout can need more capital despite better terminal earnings.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Execution has positives: the business adapted toward franchise operations, sales increased and the June/July 2026 capital receipts are documented. There is no basis to call proposed shares or warrants cash before their actual receipt dates. The equity issue delivered ₹21.08964 crore rather than its original ₹30.81 crore target; the smaller actual funding must govern expansion assumptions.

Stewardship concerns are repeated disclosure weaknesses, not a proven allegation. Bank-return verification, audit-trail evidence, ageing schedules and intangible amortisation are material for a retail business carrying ₹52.3114 crore inventory and ₹18.1141 crore receivables. A clean opinion cannot cancel contrary annexure language. Management says debtor balances are good, transactions genuine and no inventory discrepancies found; those responses are recorded but need independent support.

The related NSB BPO Solutions transaction described as purchases/net of advances totals ₹24.6201 crore. The FY27 RPT authority up to ₹50 crore is a ceiling, not a completed transaction or cash outflow. Three executive directors together received ₹1.058 crore remuneration. Neither fact alone proves unfair treatment, but supplier pricing, advances, outstanding balances and minority safeguards should be reconciled. Promoter percentage changes caused by dilution must not be mislabeled promoter selling without transaction evidence.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The main FY26 opinion and IFC report are unmodified; CARO explicitly relies on management for physical inventory and cannot determine whether 10% discrepancies exist or comment on bank stock statements versus actual stock. FY25 also had incomplete bank-return information and an audit-trail software disclaimer. FY26 does not provide clear remediation evidence. No quantified bank discrepancy is invented. CARO reports no fraud/default and no 12-month survival uncertainty, which are important counterpoints but not a verification cure.

FY23 PAT includes ₹13 crore noncash CCD waiver. The capital history identifies debt and preference/loan conversions as noncash, so reported ₹104.4 crore share issuance and ₹111.4 crore debt reduction cannot be treated as cash. A ₹6 crore movement remains unresolved. Annual versus prospectus profit/CFO differences are retained, with a conservative waiver-excluded cash diagnostic rather than a falsely complete correction.

FY25 CFO includes ₹10.151 crore external short-term financing after the ₹0.877 crore related loan was reclassified long term. FY26 CFO includes a ₹1.3529 crore short-debt reduction. Removing financing and then deducting financing-classified interest yields FY24-₹24.7108 crore, FY25-₹5.6048 crore and FY26+₹4.8519 crore. This is why reported PAT is a poor cash proxy.

Intangibles are tested at 5/10/15-year lives. No illustrative amortisation is treated as an actual cash repayment, and it is not deducted twice in CFO. FY26 zero current tax reflects carried losses; deferred tax credits are not cash earnings, so future scenarios use 25% cash tax. FD interest is excluded from operating EBIT. Known accrued statutory dues ₹0.149943504 crore and CSR ₹0.2512 crore are settled once outside modeled operating liabilities; TDS demand ₹0.565296 crore, unprovided MSME interest and unsegregated gratuity/legacy claims are separately identified or stressed. Cash on hand dominates March cash; FD ₹4.15 crore is excluded from freely available base cash without proof of lien/maturity.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the stale official 15 October close ₹251 and current 7,000,512 shares, reference market capitalization is ₹175.7129 crore. Using historical 5,648,612 shares would understate it at ₹141.7802 crore. Current-share reportedFY26P/E is 16.31×, while 25%tax and illustrative 10-year amortisation raises normalizedP/E to 30.13×. The mixed-date EV/postrent operating EBITDA is 12.02× using March debt/cash and excluding uncertainFD. This is a dated cross-check, not current cash-adjusted fair value.

The primary valuation is postrent EV/EBITDA with an explicit debt, reserve, share and available-cash bridge. Rent remains in earnings and cashflow; no hypothetical operating lease debt is added. Unspent earmarked pools and unavailableFD are excluded from terminal equity, as are any proceeds after 20 October 2031. No dividend is counted twice. Ongoing maintenance and expansion capex are funded throughout; terminal capitalization does not add a second value for operating property or inventory.

Conditional base terminal price is ₹387.06; its five-year return is 9.05% and 15% conditional hurdle price ₹192.46. These values are suppressed if any required funding interval breaches the reserve. All ordinary returns and entry prices remainNS becauseG2Hold. Bear and faster-rollout bull paths can fail even when their terminal equity arithmetic is positive. Explicit rescue alternatives pre-fund intervals with whole shares, fees and ownership dilution and are not historical facts.

Two-way tests cover new store equivalents versus multiple, working-capital intensity versus opening capex, rent escalation versus gross margin, reserve versusFD availability, repayment timing versusGCP eligibility, and TDS/legacy obligations. Hurdles 12/15/18% and optional warrant exercise are included. Reverse expectations require a finite funded sign-changing bracket; a failed bracket staysNS. Transaction spreads/impact are unverified: a 1% or 2% terminal-value haircut is a cost sensitivity, not a claim that SME liquidity is executable at those costs.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The adverse sequence is mundane but dangerous: thin gross margin compresses, inventory turns slow or stock proves impaired, franchise/customer receivables collect later, and suppliers demand cash. Rising sales then require more cash rather than releasing it. If short debt matures before operating cash or permitted object funding is available, another equity issue or stalled expansion follows. A recovery in terminal EBITDA does not cure a pre-terminal financing gap.

Book value is not a liquidation floor. Intangibles may have little sale value, inventory can need markdowns and receivables lack ageing. Property or operational assets already represented in earnings cannot be added again to EV. The report models inventory replacement cash shocks, slower collection and additional legacy claims, rather than declaring those losses already observed. Reserves are analyst safeguards, not statutory requirements or proof that a company default occurred.

Base counterevidence matters: genuine equity receipts reduce reliance on bank rollover, grocery demand persists, FY26 adjusted cash improves, no current debt default is reported and management expects favorable TDS rectification. The negative thesis would weaken with independent stock/ageing verification and several periods of normalized positive free cash. It would strengthen if advances or related balances cannot be reconciled, unsupported asset balances persist or new capital merely finances old obligations.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A five-year5× price requires about 38% annual growth and10× about 58.5%, before dividends. These are per-share outcomes, not company revenue or enterprise-value multiples. A growing store count does not automatically produce them when working capital and opening costs consume cash and new equity expands shares.

The embedded tests solve required store-equivalent expansion at the base margin, rent, capex, working-capital and terminal multiple assumptions, checking funding at every interval. They retain the funded bracket or an explicit no-solution result. Optional warrant exercise and counterfactual rescue shares dilute the existing owner’s claim while adding only actual modeled net cash. Lower terminal multiples are included, so the thesis does not depend solely on rerating.

No verified local addressable-market denominator, mature-store payback or current rollout pipeline establishes the market share needed for such outcomes. The appropriate classification is Speculative / unsupported, not a precise success probability. A future claim would require a substantially stronger verified cash engine, successful repeat cohorts, financing within minority-friendly terms and a credible path to the required diluted per-share earnings.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before reconsideration: obtain an independent physical inventory/valuation report and reconcile the bank stock statements; require debtor/payable ageing and subsequent cash collections; obtain a corrected AS26 useful-life policy with quantified historical/current effects; document audit-trail installation, full-period operation and preservation. These are G2 clearance items, not optional management-presentation improvements.

At the next half-year and annual reporting dates, track sales growth by existing/new store or a credible equivalent bridge, gross margin, shrinkage, franchise commission, rent, supplier advances, inventory/receivable days and financing-neutral postinterest CFO. Alert on renewed negative cash despite growth, rising overdue balances, reduced supplier credit or gross-margin compression greater than 100 basis points. Thresholds are analyst monitoring triggers, not company covenants.

For funding, reconcile receipts to object-wise use and cash, bank debt maturity, statutory dues, CSR/gratuity and FD liens. Monitor the ₹60.4 crore program’s intendedMarch 2028 timeline and whether the smaller actual issue leads to a formally revised plan. Warrant deadline 9 January 2028 is optional investor exercise, not assured liquidity. Before any trade verify fresh quote, restrictions, lot 300, depth and position-relative exit capacity. A single apparently attractive price does not override failed reliability evidence.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: research/watchlist only, financial-reliability Hold, not a demonstrated compounder and not investment-rank eligible. No buy/sell execution or portfolio allocation is recommended from this dossier. BQS/GQS/IAS stayNS, with disclosed exact diagnostic bounds and the weak-cash GQS ceiling. No missing factor is silently replaced with an average.

Revisit only after independent G2 evidence, credible object-wise funding and current market validation. If those conditions resolve, rerun the same operating definitions, capital bridge and downside scenarios rather than retrofitting the hurdle to the market price. A lower quote alone cannot fix unverified inventory, unsupported amortisation policy or a funding interval failure.

The constructive case is a regional grocery franchise network with real sales momentum and fresh equity. The limiting case is capital-intensive inventory and advances, low normalized returns and repeated disclosure gaps. Both belong in the assessment. Conditional model prices are sensitivity outputs, not observable fair values, and ordinary investment conclusions remain withheld.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources include fullFY26/FY25/FY24 annual reports, the signed IPO prospectus/restated financials, earlier annual archives, investor presentations, June/July allotment outcomes, EGM/corrigendum objects, official dated NSE market archives/master, notifiedAS26 text and primary peer reports. Source URLs, dates/periods, locators and available original SHA 256 hashes are retained. Earlier scanned annual archives are not presented as fully transcribed when signed restatements provide the controlling numbers.

Material unresolved questions: actual current stock and ageing; bank-return reconciliation; audit-trail remediation; intangible useful lives and prior impairment/amortisation; FY23 noncash ₹6 crore bridge; object-wise use of partial funding; latest store openings/closures and cohort productivity; bank maturities, FD availability and unfunded gratuity; CSR narrative/provision difference; current restrictions and four missing market rows. The model does not manufacture answers.

All historical, cash normalization, capital, scenario, interval, rescue, sensitivity and market observation rows are embedded in the canonical record. Companion code reconstructs calculations from authored safe extracts without raw shareholder records or personal identifiers. Reproduction verifies the calculations and selected facts, not an independent re-authentication of original source documents. This is research as of 20 October 2026; later information requires a dated update and renewed gate review.

summary:
On Door is a growing regional grocery retailer, not a demonstrated capital-light compounding platform. FY2026 sales reached ₹320.46 crore, but the most important question is whether reported inventory, receivables and earnings support reliable cash economics. The clean main audit and IFC opinion coexist with explicit CARO verification limitations and an intangible accounting policy that is inconsistent with the stated AS26 basis. This is sufficient for a financial-reliability Hold, not an allegation of fraud.

No ordinary expected return, entry price or investment ranking is assigned. BQS, Growth Quality Score and Investment Attractiveness Score are NS because critical factors remain unscored. CASH is 1 and a persistent weak-cash ceiling of 5 applies to the GQS diagnostic bound. The ₹251 official close is dated 15 October 2026, not an authenticated 20 October executable price.

Known funding is real: ₹21.08964 crore equity and ₹7.8 crore warrant upfront receipts in June/July 2026. That supports a cautious plan, but not an assumption that the entire ₹60.4 crore proposed program or optional ₹23.4 crore warrant balance is already financed. The conditional base model ends at ₹387.06 per share, with return 9.05% only if all financial-reliability premises resolve and every required interval funds. This is not a buy recommendation.
